Assignment 5: Internet Resource Guide

For this assignment, you will become familiar with online communication resources relevant to your field, such as research tools, discussion groups, writing references, information portals, and other Internet sites that members of your field find useful. You will present and describe these resources in a guide for a specific purpose for certain other members of your field, focusing on specialist-to-specialist communication.

You will design your guide as an online document that lives on the web. We will use the Penn State WordPress installation (sites.psu.edu) as our design platform. There are help resources at Penn State and your website will have a Penn State URL, which adds institutional value to a writing sample. Additionally, there are no ads on WordPress.

Objectives for this assignment include becoming familiar with specific and good communication resources used by professionals in your field; identifying possible sources of information for the work you will do in your field; making decisions about organization, design, and style as a means of creating a usable guide (with multiple parts) for readers; learning how to write abstracts; learning how to design technical communication for the web; and understanding genre conventions.

Examples of ways to focus the guide for specific audiences and purposes

A guide that helps students

  • succeed in a particular course or lab at Penn State
  • produce a capstone project or honors thesis in a particular major
  • prepare job-application materials for a certain type of career or job
  • create an online portfolio with writing samples
  • apply to a particular type of graduate or professional school
  • create a social-media presence for a certain type of professional
  • use the computing resources on campus in a particular major
  • use the library resources on campus in a particular major
  • understand the professional development opportunities in a particular field
  • prepare a grant, proposal, report or other document in a particular field

Resources to identify in the guide

Identify six (6) Internet sites that are relevant to your specific audience and purpose. Be sure to evaluate the quality of the information on the site as you make your decisions. Chapter 6 in your textbook says that secondary information should be accurate, unbiased, comprehensive, appropriately technical, current, and clear.

Here are some popular categories of information about online communication (don’t be limited by them):

  • news services
  • directories of information sources
  • professional portals
  • discussion groups and chat rooms
  • archives and databases
  • information on professional associations
  • sample reports, documents, and research studies
  • government documents
  • patents and intellectual property documents
  • specialized dictionaries
  • subject guides to a literature
  • indexes to a periodical literature
  • encyclopedias
  • handbooks
  • bibliographies
  • biographical references
  • potential employers and job search services
  • professional journals
  • style guides
  • institutional (Penn State) documents

Information to include about the resources

For each resource you select, provide identifying information-for example, title of the resource and the URL-in a consistent fashion. Then, describe the resource in an abstract so that readers will understand its function and scope. Be sure to make the abstract relevant to the task at hand and to your specific audience and purpose. In other words, do not write generic abstracts for anyone who might use the resource for anything.

In writing the abstracts, assume readers will ask the following questions:

  • What is this?
  • What is in it (content, scope)?
  • How is the information relevant to and useful for my specific audience and purpose?
  • What tips can help someone use the resource efficiently and effectively?

Be sure to provide a fully developed answer to each of these questions. Use examples to help you elaborate the resources for your audience. A trap in this assignment is writing superficial abstracts. Be patient as you describe the resources.

General information for the guide

Provide information about your guide and its use in an overall introduction. In technical communication, an introduction in a guide is often called front matter. If you group resources, consider creating sections in the guide and providing section introductions.

Be sure to cover these areas in your front matter. You can use them as headings (as appropriate) if you want to:

  • Landing Page (versus the cover or title page of a printed guide)
  • Table of Contents (to at least two levels)
  • What’s in the Guide (contents and scope)
  • Who the Guide is for (audience and purpose)
  • What the Guide assumes users know (users can be experts in some areas and novices in others)
  • How the Guide is organized for use
  • Tips for using the Guide

Website specifications

You will design your guide as an online document that lives on the web. You will therefore need to employ technical communication conventions that have been developed for the web. The following principles (discussed in the textbook) can help you design a website that supports users of the guide:

  • Use design to emphasize important information
  • Create informative headers and footers
  • Help users navigate the document
  • Include extra features users might need
  • Help users connect with others (if appropriate)
  • Design for accessibility
  • Design for multicultural readers

Technology Infrastructure

  • MS Word for composing
  • Canvas for file sharing
  • E-book for reading
  • Google or other search engine for research
  • CoPilot for research and draft support (not drafting)
  • Adobe Express for image editing (if needed)
  • WordPress for document delivery

Evaluation criteria

I will evaluate the guides according to these expectations:

Content: The guide is complete, including all necessary information, and the sources are significant and current (unless they serve a historical purpose).

Organization and Design: Readers will be able to find the information they need. Related materials are grouped. The guide is “usable” according to the issues we’ve discussed this term. The guide employs technical communication conventions for the web. On both a macro (site) and micro (page) level, the design is discernible and appropriate.

Style: Abstracts give specific information in efficient sentences (don’t confuse efficiency and brevity). Abstracts have good topic sentences. The style is deductive, with advance organizers (forecasting statements) introducing information.

Audience Adaptation: The guide offers explanatory material or instructions to help the audience achieve their purpose. Abstracts are fully elaborated with the audience and purpose in mind.

Mechanics: Spelling, grammar, and punctuation are correct.
